title: Prepay Ladder & Sustained-Use Credit Model v1
body:
One-line summary:
A prototype sheet that models a ‘prepay ladder’ (3/6/12-month prepaid buckets) combined with a sustained-use credit schedule and a small spillover rebate for short-duration overages. Purpose: evaluate tradeoffs between higher up-front revenue, reduced idle risk, and customer elasticity when offering upfront discounts plus usage credits.

Model sections (spreadsheet tabs represented inline):
1) Inputs_and_Assumptions
- Global variables (single cell style):
  * Baseline on-demand GPU $/hr = 2.80
  * Target uplift for prepaid buyers (effective price reduction) = 25%
  * Expected average utilization (dedicated pool) = 62%
  * Idle cost contribution per GPU/hr = 0.40 (amortized infra + ops)
  * Attrition / churn on prepaid = 8% annualized (modeled as monthly decay)
  * Prepay ladder options = [3mo, 6mo, 12mo]
  * Minimum commit-equivalent to qualify for prepay = 40% of pool hours

- Behavioral assumptions:
  * Customers choose prepaid tier if expected monthly burn >= break-even hours for that tier (computed).
  * Elastic response: for every 10% effective discount, estimated 6% increase in hours consumed (demand elasticity).

2) Pricing_Schemes (core calculations)
Columns: Scheme | Prepay Duration | Upfront Multiplier | Effective $/hr | Sustained-Use Credit Schedule | Spillover Rebate | Notes
Rows (examples):
- Flex-3 | 3 months | 0.95x | calc = (on-demand * (1 - ladder_discount) * utilization_adj)
- Flex-6 | 6 months | 0.90x | ...
- Flex-12 | 12 months | 0.75x | includes larger sustained credit

Formulas (represented in plain text):
- Prepay_total_paid = monthly_committed_hours * effective_price/hr * months
- Effective_hourly_cost = Prepay_total_paid / (months * 730 * eligible_fraction)
- Sustained_credit_applied = tier_credit_pct * billable_hours_above_threshold
- Spillover_rebate = min(overage_hours, spillover_cap_hours) * rebate_rate

3) Sensitivity_Scenarios
- Scenario A: Conservative demand (utilization -10%), churn +5pp, idle cost unchanged.
- Scenario B: Optimistic demand (utilization +10%), churn -3pp, idle cost -10%.
- Scenario C: High volatility (monthly variance +/-25% leading to >40% months underutilized).

Sample outputs (snapshot - numbers illustrative):
- Flex-3: effective $/hr = 2.10, expected monthly revenue per customer = $38,000, estimated ROI vs on-demand = -12% (due to admin friction and churn).
- Flex-6: effective $/hr = 1.96, revenue = $72,000, idle risk reduced by 18% with smoothing policies.
- Flex-12: effective $/hr = 1.60, revenue = $140,000, but attrition sensitivity high (small churn causes big revenue volatility).

4) Unit economics slices (per-GPU view)
- Net effective margin = effective_price/hr - (idle_cost + variable_infra_cost)
- Example: 12mo tier margin = 1.60 - (0.40 + 0.50) = 0.70 $/hr gross margin before overheads.
- Payback window for acquisition credits = months_to_recover = CAC / (monthly_margin_gain)

5) Operational mechanics and edge cases
- How to measure ‘eligible_fraction’: track historical active-hours over lookback window (default 90 days) and compute the 70th percentile to avoid short spikes.
- Grace periods: allow 10% monthly overage without penalty for first 2 months, then apply spillover rebate formula.
- Early termination: customers get pro-rated sustained credits back only if churn > 60% of prepay duration; otherwise credits are forfeited to preserve economics.

6) UX/Billing implications (billing API + Console)
- Billing fields to add: prepay_bucket_id, prepay_start_ts, sustained_credit_balance, spillover_rebate_balance, prepay_tier_label.
- Console: show forecasted effective $/hr, break-even hours, and a ‘choose tier’ simulation widget.
- Notifications: month-before-expiry email + 15-day renewal window with auto-renew toggle.

7) Sensitivity table (ASCII)
Parameter 	 Low 	 Base 	 High
Utilization 	 50% 	 62% 	 75%
Churn 	 12% 	 8% 	 4%
Effective_discount(12mo) 	 20% 	 25% 	 35%
Net_monthly_margin_change(12mo) 	 -8k 	 +12k 	 +32k

8) Recommendations (short list)
- Pilot a 6-month prepaid ladder with a modest sustained-use credit (3% of monthly bill above threshold) and a capped spillover rebate to limit abuse.
- Instrument a 90-day lookback for eligibility and include a monthly forecast in Console so customers can self-diagnose underutilization.
- Use a conservative churn buffer (modeled at +5pp) when pricing the 12-month tier for the first 6 months of the pilot.
- Route larger enterprise deals into a custom reserved agreement that layers SLO guarantees rather than pure prepay discounts.

9) Next steps / action items
- Finance: produce a 24-month cashflow projection for 6mo pilot (owner: Marcus Li, due 2025-03-09).
- Eng Billing: stub API fields for prepay metadata + credit ledger (owner: Elena Gomez, due 2025-04-01).
- Product Ops: prototype the Console tier simulator in figma and run 5 customer interviews (owner: Aisha Patel, due 2025-03-20).

10) Open questions / watchlist
- Is the 10% grace window exploitable by seasonal customers who intentionally concentrate usage at month end? Need fraud rules.
- How to reconcile prepay buckets with Dedicated pools when customers run multi-region workloads? Consider regionalized eligibility.
- Tax/accounting: recognition of prepay revenue vs delivered hours — coordinate with accounting for ASC guidance.

Notes on modeling choices:
- Chose a prepay + credit hybrid because it aligns incentives: customer gets lower per-hour cost while we protect against prolonged low utilization with credits tied to sustained usage.
- Spillover rebate is intentionally capped to avoid negative price cascades when short-term bursts exceed pool capacity and we borrow from spot.

Appendix: quick formula cheat-sheet (for engineers to port into code)
- effective_price_hr = (upfront_paid) / (max(used_hours_estimate, floor_hours_threshold))
- sustained_credit = max(0, billable_hours - credit_threshold) * credit_percent
- monthly_revenue_recognition = min(upfront_paid, recognized_by_delivery) (subject to accounting rule)

Draft notes: this is a working prototype for discussions with finance + sales. Numbers are illustrative; run a Monte Carlo (N=10k) with month-to-month hour variance to estimate tail risk before shipping any offers.

-- End of sheet draft --
